Issued at 320 AM EDT Sat Aug 29 2026

Overall no major changes in forecast thinking from the past several 
cycles. Low chances of rain showers for northern locations are 
expected tonight through Sunday.  A warming trend still remains of 
high confidence this weekend into early next week. Heat indices from 
the mid 90s to 100 are possible Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons.

An expansive low level anticyclone persists this morning from 
western New York into southern Missouri. Little movement in 
this anticyclone is expected through tonight as local area 
remains downstream of mid/upper level ridge axis across the 
Central and Northern Plains. 

A strong low level jet in vicinity of the upper level ridge axis 
across the Northern Plains has led to development of convection 
early this morning across eastern South Dakota. This convection 
should augment a smaller scale short wave progressing through this 
ridge axis, and upper level wave pattern remains supportive of 
this short wave dropping east-southeast to the southern Great 
Lakes later this afternoon/early evening. A pocket of enhanced 
mid level westerlies associated with this convectively enhanced 
short wave should shift across the southern Great Lakes region 
tonight with a period of sharp mid level moisture advection. Low
level moisture advection will be a bit more limited given what 
should remain some unfavorable low level flow trajectories 
arising from the persistence of the low level anticyclone. This 
evolution should allow for some very weak elevated instability 
to shift eastward across southern/central Lower Michigan this 
evening. Passage of this short wave, broad isentropic upglide, 
and weak elevated instability arising from elevated moisture 
transport could be enough for a few showers across the north 
tonight.

Stronger southwesterly low level flow from the Plains will migrate 
eastward to the Mid MS Valley/southern Great Lakes on Sunday with 
some increase in isentropic lift. Difficult to discern much else in 
terms of more pronounced mid/upper level forcing by this time, 
but overall pattern with advective forcing seems to support at 
least some slight chance PoPs across the northern half of the 
area. An isolated thunderstorm is possible, but better low level
moisture transport and more pronounced MUCAPEs should reside 
back across the Corn Belt. It will be noticeably warmer on 
Sunday with high temperatures into the middle 80s. With better 
moisture transport still displaced to the west, sfc dew points 
should be limited to the mid 60s locally.

For Sunday night into Monday, some subtle positive height tendencies 
are expected across the western Great Lakes downstream of more 
substantial upper trough tracking across southern 
Saskatchewan/Manitoba. Eastward progression of the upper ridge axis 
and this upper trough riding this ridge should result in some 
veering of low level flow late Monday and eastward advection of 
richer low level moisture across Corn Belt/Mid MS Valley. This 
period will also mark the beginning of a stronger mid level thermal 
ridge building across the area. A few showers and storms are 
possible as this mid level thermal ridge builds in later Monday 
night but confidence in precip is low. The main weather story for 
Tuesday/Wednesday will focus on building heat and humidity with
a potential of heat indices from the mid 90s to around 100 each
afternoon.

On Wednesday, the aforementioned upper trough will be tracking 
across the western Great Lakes and eventually eastern Great Lakes 
Wednesday evening. An associated frontal boundary may be focal point 
for isolated-scattered showers and storms somewhere across Great 
Lakes region, but questions remain as to instability magnitudes 
given presence of warm mid level thermal profiles and good 
possibility that sfc/near sfc convection is suppressed. May need
to watch for any southward migrating outflows from Great Lakes
convection aiding in convective development later Wednesday.

A period of cold advection is expected Wed night/Thu as this 
front drops into the region. Medium range guidance deterministic
solutions differ sharply by next Thu/Fri, but overall ensemble 
mean trend is for some subtle amplification of longwave western
CONUS trough-central CONUS ridge-eastern CONUS trough pattern. 
Multi-ensesmble mean position of upper ridge axis is west of the
local area which would keep greater heat concerns west of the 
local area Thursday through Saturday. However, occasional short 
waves in northwest flow aloft and potential episodes of positive
low-mid level theta-e advection accompanying these waves may 
provide some additional chances of rain in the days 5 to 7 
period.
